metadata.title: Mutually beneficial pollinator diversity and crop yield in small and large farms

summary: Global cross-farm study in Science showing establishing native floral borders and hedgerows enhances wild pollinator diversity and stabilizes crop yields.

sections.text: Crop yield gaps can be closed by enhancing wild pollinator density and species richness. Establishing non-crop flowering borders, hedgerows, and reducing pesticide applications enhances both floral resources and nesting habitat, generating positive yield and biodiversity feedback.

Continuous agricultural monocultures devoid of semi-natural vegetation suffer pollinator deficits exceeding 50%. Connecting fields via floral buffer strips restores wild bee foraging and stabilizes visitation rates across seasonal variations.
